newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse stalled ahead of U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: German bourse stalled ahead of U.S. CPI.

text.p: Uncertainty ahead of the release of December price data from the U.S. kept the German share market muted on Tuesday, with dealers predicting a sideways trend until the afternoon.
The 30-share DAX index was down 1.29 points at 2,953.66 points at 1029 GMT.
"People feel it's time for a breather now. Who knows what could happen this afternoon?," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"I think 3,000 is still a goal (for the DAX) but I don't see us taking a run at it today," he added.
March DTB DAX futures were down three points at 2,970.5.

The main excitement of the day broke minutes into bourse dealings when the government announced a new draft airline law which is expected to force Deutsche Lufthansa AG to convert all its shares to non-freely transferable shares.
Lufthansa's shares plunged as much as five percent before calming to trade at 21 marks, down nearly four percent.

Responding to the news, the airline said the government should sell its 36 percent Lufthansa stake by the end of the year and that no decision had been taken on a rights issue, prompting further concern among investors.

Chemicals group Hoechst AG also came under some pressure after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposed withdrawing its approval for its allergy drug Seldane because a safer alternative was available.
Hoechst was down 37 pfennigs at 70.03, off its lows, having led volumes for much of the session.
Overall the main focus was U.S. CPI -- a key reflection of the U.S. economic position and the outlook for interest rates, which is due for release at 1330 GMT.
